subject: Follow-up: discovery -> eval plan for streaming output coherence
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novodiagnostics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: discovery -> eval plan for streaming output coherence

Hi Samir / Nora —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all stay aligned:  

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: integrate streaming LLM responses into Novo’s triage UI for clinical notes summarization while preserving partial coherence for live preview.
- Current priority concerns: mid-stream hallucinations (partial sentences that contradict earlier context), occasional missing stop sequences when code blocks/structured lists are produced, and RTO spikes when sequence length grows.

Proposed immediate scope (for evaluation)
1) Run 1-week streaming pilot on a 2k-example prompt set (we'll provide) to measure: token-level coherence, stop-sequence reliability, 95th/99th latency under your load.
2) Baseline models to test: a smaller low-latency variant for preview (r-infer-lite-1.3) and a higher-quality variant for finalization (r-infer-3.8q).
3) Shared prompt sets + benchmark script (we'll share links and a Drive folder).

Action items / owners
- Diego: deliver prompt set and benchmark instructions by EOD today. (attachment: novo_streaming_prompt_set_v1.json)
- Laura: recommend candidate model configs and quantization trade-offs; propose canary rollout policy for streaming previews.
- Samir / Nora: confirm sample size (2k) and provide a dev endpoint + traffic profile or a replay dataset.

Timing: If we start next week, we can have initial metrics in ~7 business days.

Attaching: model_benchmarks_may2026.pdf (sample perf profiles), mutual_action_plan_Novo_20260514.xlsx (MVP scope & dates).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: discovery -> eval plan for streaming output coherence

Diego / Sergio —

I pulled together an initial model recommendation and a short checklist for the pilot. High level: prioritize a two-tier approach (preview vs finalization) and split evaluation metrics accordingly.

Quick recommendations
- Preview / live partial: r-infer-lite-1.3 (8-bit quantized) — best latency / cost. Tune: reduce decode_parallelism to 2 and enable prefix KV caching for repeated start prompts.
- Finalization / full summary: r-infer-3.8q (4-bit quantized) — better consistency for longer outputs; use strict stop-token enforcement and supervised sampling temp=0.8 for safety.

Streaming-specific knobs to include in the pilot tooling
- Incremental coherence score: compute per-chunk perplexity delta across generated chunks. Track instances where perplexity increases > 30% mid-stream.
- Stop token enforcement: test both server-side and client-side post-processing; log occurrences where stop tokens are emitted but ignored.
- Latency windows: collect p50/p95/p99 for both chunk latency and end-to-end response.

Benchmarks & prompts
- Uploaded: novo_streaming_prompt_set_v1.json (2000 prompts split by doc-type and template)
- Perf snapshot: model_benchmarks_may2026.pdf (includes seq-length scaling curves)
- Quick script: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bEvalPrompts

Risk notes
- If the preview model is too small, you’ll see coherent starts followed by degenerate tails — we should flag any example where the partial preview changes entity facts after token 40.

I'll draft a short eval rubric this evening and attach it to the shared Drive. Suggest we run an initial smoke test with 200 examples before full 2k run.

Laura Bennett
Product Solutions
Redwood Inference

Diego / Laura —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple of clarifications from our side after internal sync:

1) Sample size: we can commit to the 2k prompts, but will start you with a 300-example replay (anonymized) by Monday.
2) Examples of issues we see in prod (we attached two short transcripts inline):

--- example A ---
Partial preview emitted: "Patient reports no chest pain..." then final emits: "...but later reported chest pain that began yesterday."
--- example B ---
Streaming preview truncates list items so the client shows: "Allergic to: penicillin, sulfa" while final includes: "..., and contrast dye" (missing trailing token because of stop-token mismatch).

3) Latency: our live UI requires chunk latency <120ms for first 3 chunks, and end-to-end finalization <800ms for small docs.

Questions:
- Can you include config permutations for stop_token enforcement in the initial pilot (server-side strict vs permissive)?
- Can you surface examples where entity-level contradictions occur mid-stream? That will help our clinical team triage risk.

We will upload replay files to the Drive folder and share access early Monday. Appreciate the smoke-test approach.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product
Novo Diagnostics

Subject: RE: Follow-up: discovery -> eval plan for streaming output coherence

Samir / Nora —

Excellent — thanks for the concrete examples and the latency targets. Short replies to your questions and next steps.

1) Stop-token permutations: yes — we'll run three modes in the smoke run (server-strict, server-permissive with client post-filter, hybrid where server emits markers + client enforces). Laura will include the logging hooks so we can count mismatch incidents.

2) Entity-contradiction surface: we’ll instrument an entity-consistency check (NER match + semantic similarity) and flag any example where a named entity's canonical span changes between chunk 1 and final output. We’ll include these flagged examples in the report with token-level diffs.

3) Pilot cadence & timeline
- Mon (05/17): you upload 300 anonymized replay examples to the Drive folder.
- Tue (05/18): smoke run (200 examples, three stop-token modes) -> quick pass metrics by EOD.
- Wed-Fri (05/19-05/21): full 2k run and final report early next week.

4) Owners
- Diego: coordinate runs and deliver results to your team.
- Laura: deliver suggested config file and eval rubric by Monday morning.
- Sergio: I'll loop you for any perf-tuning and probability-of-degeneration thresholds.

I attached the mutual action plan and the initial prompt set. If this looks good, please confirm by reply and share the replay folder access so we can schedule the smoke run.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
